#### `setFeeRecipient`

```solidity
function setFeeRecipient(address newFeeRecipient) external onlyOwner;
```

Sets `newFeeRecipient` as `feeRecipient` of the fee.

> [!WARNING]
> If the fee recipient is set to the zero address, fees will accrue there and will be lost.

Modifying the fee recipient will allow the new recipient to claim any pending fees not yet accrued. To ensure that the current recipient receives all due fees, accrue interest manually prior to making any changes.

<a id="lidolend-function-createmarket-8c1358a2"></a>
<a id="lidolend-function-createmarket-marketparams"></a>

#### `createMarket`

```solidity
function createMarket(MarketParams memory marketParams) external onlyOwner;
```

Creates the market `marketParams`.

Here is the list of assumptions on the market's dependencies (tokens, IRM and oracle) that guarantees Morpho behaves as expected:

- The token should be ERC-20 compliant, except that it can omit return values on `transfer` and `transferFrom`.
- The core's token balance should not decrease except through a transfer requested by the core. Arbitrary burns, negative rebases, and similar balance changes are not supported.
- The token should not re-enter Morpho on `transfer` nor `transferFrom`.
- A successful `transfer` or `transferFrom` should decrease the sender's balance and increase the receiver's balance by exactly the requested amount. In particular, tokens with transfer fees are not supported.
- The IRM should not re-enter Morpho.
- The oracle should return a strictly positive price with the correct scaling.
- The oracle price should not be able to change instantly such that the new price is less than the old price multiplied by LLTV*LIF. In particular, if the loan asset is a vault that can receive donations, the oracle should not price its shares using the AUM.

Here is a list of assumptions on the market's dependencies which, if broken, could break Morpho's liveness properties (funds could get stuck):

- The token should not revert on `transfer` and `transferFrom` if balances and approvals are right.
- The amount of assets supplied and borrowed should not be too high (max ~1e32), otherwise the number of shares might not fit within 128 bits.
- The IRM should not revert on `borrowRate`.
- The IRM should not return a very high borrow rate (otherwise the computation of `interest` in `_accrueInterest` can overflow).
- The oracle should not revert `price`.
- The oracle should not return a very high price (otherwise the computation of `maxBorrow` in `_isHealthy` or of `assetsRepaid` in `liquidate` can overflow).

The borrow share price of a market with less than 1e4 assets borrowed can be decreased by manipulations, to the point where `totalBorrowShares` is very large and borrowing overflows.

> [!WARNING]
> Can only be called by the owner. The created market has no controller; see the overload in `ILidoLend`.

<a id="lidolend-function-createmarket-bee60e2e"></a>
<a id="lidolend-function-createmarket-marketparams-address-bool"></a>

#### `createMarket`

```solidity
function createMarket(
    MarketParams memory marketParams,
    address controller,
    bool enableSettlement
) external onlyOwner;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `marketParams` | `MarketParams` | The market to create. |
| `controller` | `address` | The non-zero controller to bind to the market. |
| `enableSettlement` | `bool` | Whether `settle` is enabled on the market. |

Creates the market `marketParams` with `controller` bound and, if `enableSettlement`, `settle` enabled.

> [!WARNING]
> This function is `onlyOwner`, and the single-argument `createMarket` is the only way to create a market without a controller.

`controller` must implement `ILidoLendMarketController` and return the new market id from `marketId()`.

The dependency assumptions documented on `IMorphoBase.createMarket` also apply to this overload.

The current implementation exposes no setter for the controller or settlement flag. A core upgrade can change either value.

#### `supply`

```solidity
function supply(
    MarketParams memory marketParams,
    uint256 assets,
    uint256 shares,
    address onBehalf,
    bytes calldata data
) external returns (uint256, uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `marketParams` | `MarketParams` | The market to supply assets to. |
| `assets` | `uint256` | The amount of assets to supply. |
| `shares` | `uint256` | The amount of shares to mint. |
| `onBehalf` | `address` | The address that will own the increased supply position. |
| `data` | `bytes` | Arbitrary data to pass to the `onMorphoSupply` callback. Pass empty data if not needed. |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<none>` | `uint256` | assetsSupplied The amount of assets supplied. |
| `<none>` | `uint256` | sharesSupplied The amount of shares minted. |

Supplies `assets` or `shares` on behalf of `onBehalf`, optionally calling back the caller's `onMorphoSupply` function with the given `data`.

Either `assets` or `shares` should be zero. Most use cases should rely on `assets` as an input so the caller is guaranteed to have `assets` tokens pulled from their balance, but the possibility to mint a specific amount of shares is given for full compatibility and precision.

Supplying a large amount can revert for overflow.

Supplying an amount of shares may lead to supply more or fewer assets than expected due to slippage. Consider using the `assets` parameter to avoid this.

> [!WARNING]
> On a controlled market, this function calls the controller's `Supply` hook after interest accrual and before the supply-specific state changes. Every call that reaches hook dispatch checks the global hook lock, including calls on markets without a controller. The controller may revert to reject the action.

```solidity
function withdraw(
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |

Withdraws `assets` or `shares` on behalf of `onBehalf` and sends the assets to `receiver`.

<a id="lidolend-function-settle-b46b73cf"></a>
<a id="lidolend-function-settle-marketparams-uint256-address-address-address"></a>
<a id="lidolend-settle"></a>

#### `settle`

```solidity
function settle(
    MarketParams memory marketParams,
    uint256 borrowShares,
    address onBehalf,
    address borrower,
    address receiver
) external returns (uint256 seizedAssets, uint256 borrowAssetsCanceled, uint256 borrowSharesCanceled, uint256 supplySharesBurned);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `marketParams` | `MarketParams` | The market to settle on. |
| `borrowShares` | `uint256` | The exact amount of `borrower`'s debt shares to cancel. |
| `onBehalf` | `address` | The address of the owner of the supply position. |
| `borrower` | `address` | The address of the owner of the debt position. |
| `receiver` | `address` | The address that will receive the seized collateral. |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The collateral seized and sent to `receiver`, priced from the shares rounded down. |
| `borrowAssetsCanceled` | `uint256` | The debt canceled, in loan-token assets, priced from the shares rounded up. This may exceed the market's pre-settlement `totalBorrowAssets` by one raw unit; the total is floored at zero. |
| `borrowSharesCanceled` | `uint256` | The count of `borrower`'s debt shares canceled. |
| `supplySharesBurned` | `uint256` | The amount of `onBehalf`'s supply shares burned. |

Cancels `borrower`'s debt shares against `onBehalf`'s supply shares and seizes the corresponding collateral to `receiver`.

Cancels exactly `borrowShares` and derives the debt assets and supply-share burn with upward rounding.

The collateral output first values the canceled debt shares with downward rounding and then converts that loan-token amount to collateral with another downward rounding. The first difference is at most one raw loan-token unit. The second is less than one raw collateral-token unit, whose loan-token value is not generally bounded by one raw loan-token unit.

A settlement whose calculated collateral output is zero reverts, unless the input is the borrower's entire debt-share balance: a settlement may close such a holding, but may never take a smaller input from one. The settling side then burns supply for the canceled debt and receives no collateral.

Passing the borrower's entire debt-share balance removes it exactly if all derived amount guards and the controller hook pass.

`msg.sender` must be authorized to manage `onBehalf`'s positions.

Settlement must be enabled on the market.

The derived supply-share burn cannot exceed `onBehalf`'s owned supply shares.

> [!WARNING]
> This function calls the controller's `Settle` hook after interest accrual and before the settlement-specific state changes. It reverts when called from any controller hook, and the controller may revert to reject the settlement.

#### `liquidate`

```solidity
function liquidate(
    MarketParams memory marketParams,
    address borrower,
    uint256 seizedAssets,
    uint256 repaidShares,
    bytes calldata data
) external returns (uint256, uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `marketParams` | `MarketParams` | The market of the position. |
| `borrower` | `address` | The owner of the position. |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The amount of collateral to seize. |
| `repaidShares` | `uint256` | The amount of shares to repay. |
| `data` | `bytes` | Arbitrary data to pass to the `onMorphoLiquidate` callback. Pass empty data if not needed. |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<none>` | `uint256` | The amount of assets seized. |
| `<none>` | `uint256` | The amount of assets repaid. |

Liquidates the given `repaidShares` of debt asset or seize the given `seizedAssets` of collateral on the given market `marketParams` of the given `borrower`'s position, optionally calling back the caller's `onMorphoLiquidate` function with the given `data`.

Either `seizedAssets` or `repaidShares` should be zero.

Seizing more than the collateral balance will underflow and revert without any error message.

Repaying more than the borrow balance will underflow and revert without any error message.

An attacker can front-run a liquidation with a small repay making the transaction revert for underflow.

> [!WARNING]
> On a controlled market, this function calls the controller's `Liquidate` hook after interest accrual and before the liquidation-specific state changes. Every call that reaches hook dispatch checks the global hook lock, including calls on markets without a controller. The controller may reject the action.

#### `flashLoan`

```solidity
function flashLoan(address token, uint256 assets, bytes calldata data) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | `address` | The token to flash loan. |
| `assets` | `uint256` | The amount of assets to flash loan. |
| `data` | `bytes` | Arbitrary data to pass to the `onMorphoFlashLoan` callback. |

Executes a flash loan.

Flash loans have access to the whole balance of the contract (the liquidity and deposited collateral of all markets combined, plus donations).

> [!WARNING]
> Not ERC-3156 compliant but compatibility is easily reached:

- `flashFee` is zero.
- `maxFlashLoan` is the token's balance of this contract.
- The receiver of `assets` is the caller.

> [!WARNING]
> This function does not dispatch a controller hook or check the global hook lock. A controller can call it while another hooked action is waiting for that controller to return.

#### `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR`

```solidity
function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() public view returns (bytes32);
```

The EIP-712 domain separator.

The separator is recomputed from the current chain id and `address(this)` on every call.

> [!WARNING]
> The domain does not distinguish deployments that have both the same chain id and the same contract address. Nonce state and authorization deadlines still apply.

#### `accrueInterest`

```solidity
function accrueInterest(MarketParams memory marketParams) external;
```

Accrues interest for the given market `marketParams`.

> [!WARNING]
> On a controlled market, this function calls the controller's `AccrueInterest` hook before accruing interest. Every call that reaches hook dispatch checks the global hook lock, including calls on markets without a controller. The controller may revert to reject the action.

It has the power to set fees on markets and set the fee recipient.

<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller"></a>

## `ILidoLendMarketController`

Interface that the controller of a market must implement.

<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-functions"></a>

### Functions

<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-function-marketid-6ed71ede"></a>
<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-function-marketid"></a>
<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-marketid"></a>

#### `marketId`

```solidity
function marketId() external view returns (Id);
```

The market id reported by this controller when it is bound.

The core checks this value during market creation. It does not revalidate it on hooks or prevent a mutable controller from being bound to more than one market.

<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-function-on-27aeba67"></a>
<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-function-on-id-hookevent-bytes"></a>
<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-on"></a>

#### `on`

```solidity
function on(Id id, HookEvent hookEvent, bytes calldata data) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `Id` | The id of the market the action is performed on. |
| `hookEvent` | `HookEvent` | The action being performed. |
| `data` | `bytes` | The abi-encoded hook payload: the `HookData` struct corresponding to `hookEvent`. |

Called by the core on each action listed in `HookEvent`, before the requested action's own state changes.

Most actions accrue interest before this call, so the hook can observe accrual writes. `AccrueInterest` dispatches before accrual, and `SupplyCollateral` does not accrue.

This interface does not authenticate the caller. A production controller that trusts the payload or changes state must require `msg.sender` to be the expected core contract.

```solidity
    Borrow,

    SupplyCollateral,

    Settle
}

```

**Fields**

| `borrower` | `address` | The position being liquidated. |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The collateral-token amount seized, after resolution. |

<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-struct-settlehookdata"></a>
<a id="ilidolendmarketcontroller-settlehookdata"></a>

#### `SettleHookData`

```solidity
struct SettleHookData {
    address caller;
    address onBehalf;
    address borrower;
    address receiver;
    uint256 supplySharesBurned;
    uint256 borrowAssetsCanceled;
    uint256 borrowSharesCanceled;
    uint256 seizedAssets;
}
```

Payload for the `Settle` hook.

> [!WARNING]
> `borrowAssetsCanceled` can exceed the market's `totalBorrowAssets` by one raw loan-token unit. The core floors the new total at zero, so a controller reconstructing post-settlement state must do the same.

> [!WARNING]
> `seizedAssets` applies two downward roundings: debt-share valuation and loan-to-collateral conversion. Only the first difference is bounded by one raw loan-token unit. The second is less than one raw collateral-token unit, whose loan-token value depends on token decimals and the oracle price.

**Fields**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caller` | `address` | The settle call's msg.sender. |
| `onBehalf` | `address` | The address whose supply shares are burned. |
| `borrower` | `address` | The address whose debt is canceled and collateral seized. |
| `receiver` | `address` | The address receiving the seized collateral. |
| `supplySharesBurned` | `uint256` | The supply shares burned from onBehalf, after resolution. |
| `borrowAssetsCanceled` | `uint256` | The loan-token debt canceled, computed by pricing the canceled shares up. |
| `borrowSharesCanceled` | `uint256` | The borrow shares burned from borrower, computed in core. |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The collateral-token amount seized, computed by pricing the canceled shares down and then converting the result to collateral with downward rounding. Warning: it is zero when the input closes a holding worth less than one raw collateral unit, the only settlement the core admits with no collateral output. A controller that divides by this value must handle zero, and one that drains its own books by it must skip that call. A controller that rejects such a settlement leaves the holding open, and only `repay` or `liquidate` can clear it then. |

| `borrower` | `address` | The borrower of the position. |
| `repaidAssets` | `uint256` | The amount of assets repaid. May be 1 over the corresponding market's `totalBorrowAssets`. |
| `repaidShares` | `uint256` | The amount of shares burned. |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The amount of collateral seized. |
| `badDebtAssets` | `uint256` | The amount of assets of bad debt realized. |
| `badDebtShares` | `uint256` | The amount of borrow shares of bad debt realized. |

<a id="eventslib-event-settle-7b99f5d40c48404b0b51a7b8694d7033c14a9726961fc462ad7fcd145f63e00b"></a>
<a id="eventslib-event-settle-id-address-address-address-address-uint256-uint256-uint256-uint256"></a>
<a id="eventslib-settle"></a>

### `Settle`

```solidity
event Settle(
    Id indexed id,
    address caller,
    address indexed onBehalf,
    address indexed borrower,
    address receiver,
    uint256 supplySharesBurned,
    uint256 borrowAssetsCanceled,
    uint256 borrowSharesCanceled,
    uint256 seizedAssets
);
```

Emitted on a successful `settle`.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `Id` | The market id. |
| `caller` | `address` | The caller of `settle`. |
| `onBehalf` | `address` | The supply-side account whose shares are burned. |
| `borrower` | `address` | The borrower whose debt and collateral are reduced. |
| `receiver` | `address` | The address that received the seized collateral. |
| `supplySharesBurned` | `uint256` | The supply shares burned from `onBehalf`. |
| `borrowAssetsCanceled` | `uint256` | The upward-rounded asset value derived from the canceled borrower shares. The core uses it for the supply reduction and the zero-floored reduction of total borrow assets. |
| `borrowSharesCanceled` | `uint256` | The borrow shares burned from `borrower`. |
| `seizedAssets` | `uint256` | The collateral seized from `borrower` and sent to `receiver`. |

<a id="errorslib-errors"></a>

## Errors (`ErrorsLib`)

| Constant | Revert string | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="errorslib-not-owner"></a>`NOT_OWNER` | `"not owner"` | Thrown when the caller is not the owner. |
| <a id="errorslib-max-lltv-exceeded"></a>`MAX_LLTV_EXCEEDED` | `"max LLTV exceeded"` | Thrown when market creation uses an LLTV greater than or equal to WAD. |
| <a id="errorslib-max-fee-exceeded"></a>`MAX_FEE_EXCEEDED` | `"max fee exceeded"` | Thrown when the fee to set exceeds the maximum fee. |
| <a id="errorslib-already-set"></a>`ALREADY_SET` | `"already set"` | Thrown when the value is already set. |
| <a id="errorslib-market-already-created"></a>`MARKET_ALREADY_CREATED` | `"market already created"` | Thrown when the market is already created. |
| <a id="errorslib-no-code"></a>`NO_CODE` | `"no code"` | Thrown when a token to transfer doesn't have code. |
| <a id="errorslib-market-not-created"></a>`MARKET_NOT_CREATED` | `"market not created"` | Thrown when the market is not created. |
| <a id="errorslib-inconsistent-input"></a>`INCONSISTENT_INPUT` | `"inconsistent input"` | Thrown when not exactly one of the input amounts is zero. |
| <a id="errorslib-zero-assets"></a>`ZERO_ASSETS` | `"zero assets"` | Thrown when zero assets is passed as input. |
| <a id="errorslib-zero-address"></a>`ZERO_ADDRESS` | `"zero address"` | Thrown when a zero address is passed as input. |
| <a id="errorslib-unauthorized"></a>`UNAUTHORIZED` | `"unauthorized"` | Thrown when the caller is not authorized to conduct an action. |
| <a id="errorslib-insufficient-collateral"></a>`INSUFFICIENT_COLLATERAL` | `"insufficient collateral"` | Thrown when the collateral is insufficient to `borrow` or `withdrawCollateral`. |
| <a id="errorslib-insufficient-liquidity"></a>`INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` | `"insufficient liquidity"` | Thrown when the liquidity is insufficient to `withdraw` or `borrow`. |
| <a id="errorslib-healthy-position"></a>`HEALTHY_POSITION` | `"position is healthy"` | Thrown when the position to liquidate is healthy. |
| <a id="errorslib-invalid-signature"></a>`INVALID_SIGNATURE` | `"invalid signature"` | Thrown when the authorization signature is invalid. |
| <a id="errorslib-signature-expired"></a>`SIGNATURE_EXPIRED` | `"signature expired"` | Thrown when the authorization signature is expired. |
| <a id="errorslib-invalid-nonce"></a>`INVALID_NONCE` | `"invalid nonce"` | Thrown when the nonce is invalid. |
| <a id="errorslib-transfer-reverted"></a>`TRANSFER_REVERTED` | `"transfer reverted"` | Thrown when a token transfer reverted. |
| <a id="errorslib-transfer-returned-false"></a>`TRANSFER_RETURNED_FALSE` | `"transfer returned false"` | Thrown when a token transfer returned false. |
| <a id="errorslib-transfer-from-reverted"></a>`TRANSFER_FROM_REVERTED` | `"transferFrom reverted"` | Thrown when a token transferFrom reverted. |
| <a id="errorslib-transfer-from-returned-false"></a>`TRANSFER_FROM_RETURNED_FALSE` | `"transferFrom returned false"` | Thrown when a token transferFrom returned false |
| <a id="errorslib-max-uint128-exceeded"></a>`MAX_UINT128_EXCEEDED` | `"max uint128 exceeded"` | Thrown when the maximum uint128 is exceeded. |
| <a id="errorslib-controller-mismatch"></a>`CONTROLLER_MISMATCH` | `"controller mismatch"` | Thrown when a controller is bound whose `marketId` does not match the market. |
| <a id="errorslib-settlement-disabled"></a>`SETTLEMENT_DISABLED` | `"settlement disabled"` | Thrown when `settle` is called on a market that did not opt into it. |
| <a id="errorslib-settlement-exceeds-supply"></a>`SETTLEMENT_EXCEEDS_SUPPLY` | `"settlement exceeds supply"` | Thrown when settlement would burn more supply shares than `onBehalf` owns. |
| <a id="errorslib-settlement-slice-too-small"></a>`SETTLEMENT_SLICE_TOO_SMALL` | `"settlement slice too small"` | Thrown when the settlement borrow-share input is zero or its calculated collateral output is zero. |
| <a id="errorslib-settlement-exceeds-collateral"></a>`SETTLEMENT_EXCEEDS_COLLATERAL` | `"settlement exceeds collateral"` | Thrown when settlement would seize more than the borrower's collateral. |
| <a id="errorslib-settlement-exceeds-debt"></a>`SETTLEMENT_EXCEEDS_DEBT` | `"settlement exceeds debt"` | Thrown when settlement would cancel more than the borrower's debt shares. |
| <a id="errorslib-already-initialized"></a>`ALREADY_INITIALIZED` | `"already initialized"` | Thrown when `initialize` is called after the contract is already initialized. |
| <a id="errorslib-hook-reentrancy"></a>`HOOK_REENTRANCY` | `"hook reentrancy"` | Thrown when a hooked action is reentered while a controller hook is executing. |
